questions.stemHtml: If a tumor compresses the structures passing through the opening marked in the given image, which of the following sensations would be affected?

options.label: C
options.text: Sensation in the anterior scalp and dorsum of the nose

questions.answerText: Sensation in the anterior scalp and dorsum of the nose
questions.solutionHtml:
Sensation in the anterior scalp and dorsum of the nose
  • The marked foramen is superior orbital fissure. The branches of Ophthalmic nerve traverses through Superior orbital fissure.
  • The ophthalmic nerve (V1) of the trigeminal nerve provides sensory innervation to the anterior scalp and dorsum of the nose.

Structure passing through Superior orbital Fissure

questions.stem: A chronic tobacco consumer went to the dental clinic with bleeding lesions on his tongue and was diagnosed with carcinoma of the tongue. Which of the following papillae, which do not have taste buds, is least likely to be involved in such a cancer?
questions.solutionHtml:
Filiform
  • Filiform papillae do not have taste buds. They are non-taste papillae that make up the majority of the tongue's papillae and give the tongue its texture and sense of touch. Filiform papillae cover most of the tongue's front two-thirds.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 3, Page No. 300.

questions.stem: An absent gag reflex can result from injury to which of the following nerves?
questions.solutionHtml:
IX and X
  • The gag reflex, also known as the pharyngeal reflex, is an involuntary reflex that protects the throat from foreign objects:

 

The afferent and efferent nerves involved in the gag reflex are:

  • Afferent nerve- The glossopharyngeal nerve (cranial nerve IX) carries sensory information to the nucleus solitarius in the medulla oblongata.
  • This nerve supplies sensory innervation to the oropharynx.
  • Efferent nerve- The vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) carries motor information from the nucleus ambiguus in the medulla oblongata to the pharyngeal muscles.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 4, Page No. 89.

questions.stem: Which artery is used for arteriovenous shunting with the great saphenous vein for hemodialysis, and is located behind the medial malleolus and 2.5 cm in front of the tendo calcaneus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Posterior tibial artery
  • The posterior tibial artery is located behind the medial malleolus and midway between the medial malleolus and the medial border of the tendo calcaneus.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 198.

questions.stemHtml: Where will you find the epithelium shown in the image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ureter

The above image is of ureter

  • The ureter is a muscular tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, and its epithelium is made up of transitional epithelium. Transitional epithelium is a type of epithelium that has three layers:
  • Superficial layer: Contains umbrella cells
  • Intermediate layer: Contains cuboidal and low columnar cells
  • Basal layer: A single layer of cells.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 378.

questions.stem: During the examination of a patient, a professor asks the patient to invert his foot and points to a prominent tendon located behind the medial malleolus. Which tendon is being highlighted?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tibialis Posterior
  • The tendon of the tibialis posterior muscle descends posterior to the medial malleolus.



Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 128.

questions.stem: An elderly woman reports difficulty in buttoning her shirt and increased clumsiness during daily activities. On examination, she is unable to make an 'O' shape by opposing her thumb and index finger. Which of the following muscles is most likely involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
Abductor pollicis brevis
  • The above condition is caused by anterior interosseous nerve injury.
  • The OK sign test is a clinical test to evaluate for potential injury of the anterior interosseous nerve, Therefore the nerve affected can be the median nerve as it gives an anterior interosseous nerve as a branch.
  • Among the options given above , Abductor pollicis brevis is the best answer because it is supplied by only the median nerve.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 1, Page No. 138.
questions.stemHtml: An elderly woman reports difficulty in buttoning her shirt and increased clumsiness during daily activities. On examination, she is unable to make an 'O' shape by opposing her thumb and index finger. Which of the following muscles is most likely involved?

questions.solutionHtml:
Medial pectoral nerve
  • The above nerve marked in image is medial pectoral nerve because, The medial pectoral nerve originates from the medial cord of the brachial plexus, and is made up of fibers from the eighth cervical and first thoracic nerve roots.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 1, Page No. 56.

questions.stem: A patient presents with sciatica and tenderness in the hamstring muscles. Which nerve supplies the hybrid muscle that is likely to be spared in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Obturator Nerve
  • The adductor portion of the adductor magnus is innervated by the posterior division of the obturator nerve (L2-L4).
  • The adductor magnus hamstring portion is so named due to its similarity in structure, proximal attachment, and innervation to the hamstring muscles.


Human Anatomy by BD Chaurasia's, 8th Edition, Volume 2, Page No. 87.
